title: How to brief a vending screen campaign
excerpt: Prepare a retail media brief covering audience, locations, screen creative, playback checks and reporting before booking.
opening: A good brief helps the media team choose machines and gives the creative team a clear job. Start with the moment you want to influence, such as an afternoon drinks purchase at an office site. Use that moment to decide whether the screen should prompt a purchase, start a trial or invite a follow-up action.
checklist: State one objective and one primary measure. Pick a metric you can collect, such as playback records, tracked page visits or units sold.
Describe the audience, areas, venue types, dates and budget. Explain which requirements are fixed and where substitutions are acceptable.
Ask whether the machine can carry the product shown. For a combined campaign, agree who stocks it, the refill plan and what to do when the row sells out.
Request screen dimensions, orientation, accepted files and duration. Design for a short glance, with one legible message and a single action.
Test the actual asset on a machine or accurate screen preview. If using a QR code, scan it from realistic distances and test the landing page on a phone.
Agree on evidence before launch. Ask what playback records, stock data and sales data can be supplied, by which dates and with which gaps disclosed.
close: Send a one-page brief, the draft asset and the desired reporting measures together. Request a shortlist with site availability and reporting confirmed per location.
